title: Bangkok Underwater: 12 Inches of Rain Floods Thailand's Capital
summary:
Imagine rain so heavy that streets turn into rivers. That's what happened in Bangkok, the capital of Thailand.

Since Thursday, more than 300 millimeters (12 inches) of rain has fallen on the city. That's like dumping a tall bucket of water on every single street. Roads are submerged, and the city's canals have burst their banks. All 50 of Bangkok's districts have been declared emergency zones.

"The water keeps coming in. It's hard to go out now. It's like at my waist level now," said Somkid Pheuk-ngam, a 67-year-old who lives near a canal north of central Bangkok. She has closed her shop for two days.

Bangkok's governor, Chadchart Sittipunt, said the east of the city was hit hardest. "The rain keeps falling and we are doing our best," he said. "We are trying to pump the water out, but the water in canals are full."

People have been told to stay home. Those living near canals should move their belongings to upper floors. So far, no deaths have been reported in Bangkok. But the weather service says more heavy rain is coming this week.
why_it_matters: Floods like this show how important drains, canals, and warning systems are — a few days of rain can close schools, shops, and roads in a big city.

The city sits on low, flat ground near a big river, so heavy rain can flood the streets quickly.
Thailand has a rainy season every year, when storms drop a lot of water in a short time.
